proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is a specific kind of legal right — the right to alienate, consume, or destroy a res — recognized within Roman property law. It is externally grounded in the social-legal practice of property recognition and attaches to a bearer (an owner/dominus) in virtue of their legal relationship to a thing. It is thus a Role (BFO_0000023), and more specifically a sub-kind of LegalRight (which is already classed as BFO_0000023 in the working ontology). As a recurring kind rather than a token instance, it is modeled as a class.

entities.label: RomanPropertyRight
entities.rationale: Roman property theory individuates the dominium bundle into usus, fructus, and abusus. RomanPropertyRight is a useful intermediate class (subclass of LegalRight) that groups these rights. Abusus, Usus, and Fructus can all be subclasses of it. This mirrors the Roman tripartite structure and preserves ontological economy. Introduced here as it is needed to situate Abusus precisely.

relations.rationale: RomanPropertyRight is a species of LegalRight; it is externally grounded (role) and inheres in an owner relative to a res under Roman law.
Abusus is the specific right of alienation/consumption/destruction within the Roman tripartite dominium, making it a sub-kind of RomanPropertyRight.

open_questions: Should we also mint sibling classes Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits) now, or handle them separately when they arise?

Should Abusus be treated as a class (the kind of right) or also as a specific individual instance within a particular legal corpus such as the Corpus Iuris Civilis? If a token instance is needed, a separate individual should be minted.

Roman dominium is often treated as a single unified role (dominium/ownership) of which usus, fructus, abusus are components or aspects. Should we model the bundle itself as a separate class (e.g., Dominium) with part-of relations to the three sub-rights, rather than a linear subclass hierarchy?

Is the bearer of Abusus always an individual person (dominus), or can it also be a corporate/collective entity? This affects whether the bearer constraint should be scoped to material entities generally or to persons specifically.
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus — the ius abutendi of Roman property law — is the right of the dominus to alienate, consume, or destroy the object of ownership. In BFO terms it is a specifically dependent continuant of the Role sub-type (BFO_0000023): it is externally grounded in the socio-legal recognition of property relations, it inheres in a single bearer (the dominus) at any time, and it is realized in acts of alienation or destruction. The working ontology already has LegalRight as a subclass of BFO_0000023, so Abusus is naturally a subclass of LegalRight. An intermediate class RomanPropertyRight is introduced to capture the broader Roman-law framework within which Abusus, Usus, and Fructus are sibling specifications of dominium, keeping the hierarchy principled and extensible. Both are modeled as classes because they denote kinds of rights rather than token role-instances borne by particular individuals.
